chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abi al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Abi 'Uyaynah, who said:
Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام was asked about a mouse that falls into a well, and he said: If it comes out, then there is no harm; but if it decomposes, then seven buckets [should be drawn].

He said: And he was asked about a mouse that falls into the well, and no one knows about it until after one has performed wudu (ablution) from it. Should he repeat his wudu (ablution) and his salat (prayer), and wash whatever it touched? He said: No. The people of the house have already used it and sprinkled with it.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being ruled upon
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةِ: a mouse, the source of contamination discussed in the ruling
key_terms.تَفَسَّخَتْ: decomposed or disintegrated in the water
key_terms.رَشُّوا: they sprinkled with it, indicating household use of the water
key_terms.سَبْعُ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets to be drawn from the well
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُ: his salat (prayer), whether it must be repeated
key_terms.وُضُوءَهُ: his wudu (ablution), whose validity is being asked about

ai.seo_question: If a mouse falls into a well, does the water invalidate wudu (ablution) and salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a mouse falling into a well and the effect that has on the well water. It also states that if the matter is only discovered after using the water for wudu (ablution) and salat (prayer), those acts do not need to be repeated.
